taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it was formerly included in the Eurasian Magpie (Pica pica) and was split on morphological, behavioural and genetic characters (AOU 2000); some authors consider it conspecific with Yellow-billed Magpie.
fieldMarks: Green and blue gloss on the wings and long tail
Big white wing patches flash in flight
behavior: Mostly a permanent resident, with some upslope movement in fall and a few moving south or downslope in winter
Forages mostly by walking on the ground, flipping items with the bill; may take ticks from elk and other animals
Omnivorous, eating more insects than most crows plus carrion, rodents, eggs and nestlings, with more berries, seeds and nuts in winter
Rapid, nasal mag? mag? mag? or yak yak yak
habitat: Semi-open country in the west: rangeland, conifers, streamsides, forest edges and farms; most common in streamside groves in open terrain. Avoids unbroken forest, treeless grasslands and extreme desert.
range: Resident from south-coastal and southern Alaska through western Canada to eastern California, southern Nevada and Utah, northern New Mexico and western Kansas and Oklahoma.

lookalikes.name: Yellow-billed magpie
lookalikes.howToTell: Found in California; the Black-billed has a black bill (Audubon says to see Yellow-billed there).
